fact: A DHIS2 Community poster (author Jean Louis Komayan) states that the Ministry of Health and Population undertook the reform of the national health information system (SNIS) and adopted DHIS2 as the national platform; no date is given for the adoption, so the document's published date is used.

The poster states that DHIS2 has been deployed in all 35 health districts, with data managers recruited and offline and VSAT solutions used for connectivity; it does not say that facilities enter their own reports, and describes reporting systems before the reform as fragmented and mostly paper.
The poster states that report completeness in DHIS2 rose from 52% in 2020 to more than 85% in 2025, across the 35 health districts.

The essay (Data Landscapers, an AI-assisted compilation) states that DHIS2 was piloted only in Bangui under the 2019 HMIS roadmap, with revised paper tools rolled out to 12 districts and no routine use in rural health centres (387 centres and 434 posts), data being transcribed upward from paper rather than captured at facilities; the statement is undated, so the published date is used.

fact: HISP Rwanda states that it is supporting deployment of the HISP EMR (e-SENI) in partnership with the Ministry of Health and the Susan Buffett Foundation, under the SENI project; no date is given, so the published date is used.

HISP Rwanda states that the e-SENI EMR gives each patient a unique identification and a centralised record captured in real time across clinical units, from registration and consultation to laboratory and pharmacy, shared within the facility and synchronised to a central EMR server; no date is given, so the published date is used.

HISP Rwanda states that its team supervised implementation of the e-SENI EMR at hospital and health centres, giving no number of sites and not stating the hospitals' level, and that medical records in many facilities are still kept in paper registers; no date is given, so the published date is used.

HISP Rwanda reports a phased deployment of the e-SENI EMR under way, with site assessments, configuration in French, staff training, an EMR showroom and a central synchronisation server set up; no event date is given, so the published date is used.

The World Bank appraisal document states that the Roadmap for the HMIS was elaborated in June 2019 and was being implemented at appraisal, and that the country's ambition is to roll out DHIS2 in all areas of the country; the published date is used for the date of that position.

The World Bank appraisal document states that the SENI-Plus project (an IDA grant of US$58 million equivalent and a Global Financing Facility grant of US$12 million) will finance the national rollout of improved HMIS tools and the gradual transition to DHIS2 in all 35 districts, IT equipment and connectivity including VSAT, and data managers in all regions and districts, building on the 55 data managers recruited under SENI.

The World Bank appraisal document states that there is no functioning HMIS, that revised paper forms and registers had been rolled out in 12 districts, that DHIS2 had been piloted in Bangui and was in only five districts in and around Bangui, and that data managers scaled it up particularly at the district level; the published date is used, the statements being undated.

The IMPULSE study (Journal of Global Health 2025) found that 21.4% of the 14 health facilities it assessed in the Central African Republic used a functional electronic system for routine data entry and analysis, against over 75% in Ethiopia, Tanzania and Uganda; the 14 were hospitals and health centres giving emergency obstetric care in Bangui and health regions 1, 2 and 7, chosen for access and security, with data collected between November 2022 and July 2024.

The IMPULSE study found a functional electronic system for data entry and analysis in 83.3% of the 6 district health offices it assessed in the Central African Republic, against 21.4% of the 14 facilities, and states that all data offices used DHIS2 for key data analysis; data collected between November 2022 and July 2024.

The Ministry of Health's routine immunisation recovery plan 2021-2022 states that the country holds a validated 2017-2021 strategic plan for strengthening the SNIS, turned into an operational plan each year, and a validated roadmap for revitalising the SNIS for the move to DHIS2; the statement is undated, so the document's published date is used.

The plan places the SNIS in the Ministry of Health and Population: it counts 9 SNIS staff among the ministry cadres to be trained and gives the ministry's SNIS service the administration of the DHIS2 system; undated, so the document's published date is used.

The plan costs 'revitalisation of the SNIS for the move to DHIS2' at 141,954,000 FCFA over six activities for 2021-2022 (configuring DHIS2 at 52,000,000 FCFA with 30,000,000 shown as available, and progressive deployment to all regions and districts), and leaves the source-of-financing column empty for every one of them; undated, so the document's published date is used.

The plan states that data managers are in post in the 35 health districts, the 7 health regions and 5 central hospitals for keying SNIS data, and refers to facilities' SNIS reports arriving at the district; undated, so the document's published date is used.

The plan names 5 central hospitals as having data managers for keying SNIS data, alongside the 35 district and 7 regional health offices; it names no other facility tier doing so; undated, so the document's published date is used.
